headline: High: gpt-engineer can write and execute code in a shared project directory, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks when paired with system_prompts_leaks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-engineer writes files in a user-specified project directory and has no self-isolation by default; system_prompts_leaks is a source-available prompt-leak corpus that can supply attacker-controlled text. If that text is placed in the shared project directory, gpt-engineer may ingest it as trusted content. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF attacker-controlled text is stored in the shared project directory before gpt-engineer reads it
IF gpt-engineer treats file contents as instructions or context without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the two agents into different directories
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted files
Add a manual review step before gpt-engineer reads any corpus content
Run gpt-engineer on a throwaway workspace
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for file inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-engineer reads and writes the project directory and can call configured model APIs; system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leak repository that may contain sensitive extracted prompts. If those files are shared into gpt-engineer's workspace, contents can flow to the model backend. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF sensitive prompt-leak artifacts are copied into gpt-engineer's project directory
IF gpt-engineer sends file contents to its configured model backend during generation
mitigations: Keep prompt-leak artifacts out of the coding workspace
Use a redacted sample instead of raw corpus files
Turn off network access during inspection runs
Review outputs before any upload step
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data classification filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-engineer has broad network egress plus filesystem write, while system_prompts_leaks is a repository of content that may be edited or mirrored into the same project directory. Shared mutable workspace access creates write-conflict risk even though agent_b itself has no explicit write capability documented. Uncertainty about agent_b's runtime surface pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory
IF system_prompts_leaks content is modified or mirrored while gpt-engineer is writing files
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize edits with a lock file
Snapshot the workspace before each run
Avoid concurrent writes to the same repo
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer can generate code and offer to run it, so its output may be treated as authoritative by downstream workflows. system_prompts_leaks is a corpus of leaked prompts, which can bias or mislead generation if fed in as context. Because the pairwise handoff is plausible but not documented, the safer medium severity is warranted.
conditions: IF gpt-engineer-generated code or claims are used downstream without verification
IF leaked prompt text is supplied as context to generation or execution
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Compare generated code against a checklist
Do not treat corpus text as ground truth
Run a dry-run only mode
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-engineer handles generated source code and an OpenAI or other configured model API, while system_prompts_leaks is source-available and not documented as handling regulated data. No residency or certification mismatch is evidenced, so only a small compliance gap is plausible if leaked prompts contain sensitive material.
conditions: IF the prompt-leak corpus contains regulated or confidential data
IF that data is processed by gpt-engineer through a third-party model API
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the corpus
Use local-only review for sensitive samples
Document retention for generated artifacts
Check vendor terms before upload
requires-engineering: add data-classification and residency controls
